query: A Satchel of Your Own There's a new satchel on your peg at the loft, with your name stitched on the flap. The chief wants to keep you on after graduation, full time, flying the lake in all weathers. "The broom still pulls left," she says. "You don't." Answer by the last day. Sling the satchel over your shoulder It fits. You fly a lap of the lake that evening for no reason at all, and the loft cheers you down. Ask about the winter routes The chief shows you the map of the winter routes, with the crosses where couriers came down. There are not many. There are some.

results.excerpt:
The Broom That Pulls Left
Your loft broom pulls left, always has. With the jar's wind behind it, it would pull you into the lake. The broom-maker in the village can true it, for a price.
